description: Synthetic evaluation cases for the Gigsie FairScope experiment. These are invented examples used to measure the draft-then-review workflow. They are not real customers, real jobs, or verified market rates.

cases.note: Well-specified request: narrow deliverables, a clear outcome, and a stated budget and deadline.

request.description: We want three Instagram images and matching captions for our new seasonal menu.
request.outcome: Regular customers see the new items and visit during the two-week menu period.
request.extra_context: We can supply photos of the new menu items taken on a phone.

cases.expect_reason: The request is specific, so FairScope should not invent a problem here. Flagging it would be a false positive.

cases.note: Well-specified request for a simple informational page with a stated budget and deadline.

request.description: We need a simple one-page website showing our subjects, our teaching hours, and a contact form link.
request.outcome: Parents who find us can see what we teach and email us for a trial lesson.
request.extra_context: Our subjects and timings are already written down in a plain text file.

cases.expect_reason: The scope is bounded and the budget is stated, so no ambiguity is expected.

cases.note: Fixed number of items, so the deliverable count is checkable.

request.description: We need short product descriptions for ten of the sarees listed in our spreadsheet.
request.outcome: Customers browsing the shop can read what each fabric feels like and how to care for it.
request.extra_context: The spreadsheet already has fabric, colour, size, and care columns filled in for most rows.

cases.expect_reason: Several rows in a real sheet are often incomplete, so the missing-information checks are expected to fire at least once.

cases.note: Mechanical, checkable work: the acceptance criterion is a row count.

request.description: Our stock sheet has duplicate rows and inconsistent date formats. Please tidy it up.
request.outcome: One row per item, with dates written the same way every time.
request.extra_context: The sheet has about 800 rows and four columns: item, quantity, date received, and location.

cases.expect_reason: The deliverable and its check are concrete, so FairScope should not flag it.

cases.note: Deliberately under-specified and over-scoped. No deliverables, no exclusions, no skills, and a broad objective. FairScope is expected to detect this.

request.description: We need help with marketing. Do whatever is needed to get us noticed online and grow the business.
request.outcome: More people find us and we get more enquiries and bookings.

cases.expect_reason: This is the positive detection case. The objective is vague, there is no deadline, no deliverables, and the request spans a whole marketing campaign. A deterministic checker must flag it.
